title: Minimum Absolute Difference in BST
summary: For a given Binary Search Tree, find the smallest absolute difference between values of any two distinct nodes.
statement: For a given Binary Search Tree, find the smallest absolute difference between values of any two distinct nodes.
constraints: 2 <= node count <= 10,000; tree height <= 200; 0 <= node.val <= 100,000; the input is a binary search tree.
Return the smallest absolute value difference between ANY TWO DISTINCT nodes, not just parent/child pairs. Equal values at distinct nodes give zero.
Do not change node values or links. Inorder values are non-decreasing; use this order rather than the JSON level-order sequence. Recursive or iterative traversal is allowed.

hints: In a sorted sequence, a closest pair appears at adjacent positions.
Inorder traversal supplies that sorted sequence without sorting or changing the tree.
Traverse left/node/right recursively or with a stack, compare each value to the previous visited value, and retain the smallest difference.
Do not confuse an adjacent inorder pair with a parent/child edge. The tree height is at most 200, so ordinary recursive inorder traversal is supported.
editorial: For sorted values a<=b<=c, c-a is at least either neighboring gap. Thus the global minimum occurs between adjacent inorder visits. Track only the previous value and best gap using recursive inorder traversal or an explicit O(h) stack. Each node is pushed and popped once, so time is O(n). The independent oracle takes every pair of non-null JSON values; it does not traverse inorder or assume the closest pair is adjacent. Input nodes and links remain unchanged.
